reporting_note: Grid operators file DOE OE-417 reports and pipeline operators file PHMSA reports, but neither covers refineries, and much of the US record still comes from press and company statements.

geography.note: 50 states and the District of Columbia. US territories (Puerto Rico and others) are outside this system's geography this iteration; their events are held in the candidate queue, not dropped. The map opens on the lower 48; Alaska and Hawaii are drawn and selectable when zoomed out.

sectors.reason: Denominator ready (EIA Refinery Capacity Report: 124 sites, exact national total). No systematic refinery-outage register and no approved recovery model. Not scored. The recovery and decay model behind the Monitored-Area ESDI was calibrated on repeated strikes with almost no restart reporting, and no model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).

Denominator ready (EIA-860M, with retirement dates back to 2002). Fossil unit outages are not public. Not scored. The recovery and decay model behind the Monitored-Area ESDI was calibrated on repeated strikes with almost no restart reporting, and no model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).

The ESDI's transmission measure counts struck substations against a saturation constant of 8; at about 229 OE-417 events a year it would read close to 100% on an ordinary day. A customer-interruption measure is a different concept and is not built.
No complete terminal and pipeline-operations denominator.
Gas splits into production, processing, pipelines, storage and LNG export, with different denominators. LNG export is the most ready; none is scored.
Mine production is published by mine; capacity only by state.

research_gaps: The first systematic sweep (iteration 16) is PARTIAL: two of its nine source lanes completed. The grid lane has no 2026 data yet (DOE has not published a 2026 OE-417 summary), so January-October 2026 grid events rest on the hazard and targeted lanes; the refinery, LNG and coal lanes are structured samples of news reporting, not censuses.

103 candidates were held, most of them OE-417 rows whose figure is an incident total rather than a peak at one time; they are not recorded until a peak figure from a utility, state agency or DOE is found.
Peak figures that rest only on an outage aggregator are held. The grandfathered Winter Storm Elliott Maine record rests on such a snapshot and is queued for re-review.
US territories are outside this system's geography: Puerto Rico events found by research are held pending an owner decision.
provenance: Authored 2026-10-30 (iteration 14) from the source-audit, readiness and incident lanes' reports. Edit by hand; this file is the curated source.
